segments.text: The goal is the manpage2 password, from /manpage/manpage1: the same strcpy overflow into a 256-byte buffer, but this time a length check fires.
If the copy reaches 255 bytes the program raises SIGTERM after the copy, killing the process before the return.

The solve is the same shellcode with the signal disarmed: the exploit child blocks SIGTERM with pthread_sigmask before the exec, so the pending raise never delivers and the corrupted return still wins. One quirk: the spawned shell dies after its first command, so each run sends exactly one.

Then the overflow runs: setresuid seventeen thousand two re-asserts manpage two, execve of slash bin slash slash sh, NOP sled first and the return address swept around 0xffffd9e8 - the hit lands at 0xffffd5e0.

I log in as manpage one, read the source, probe the offset in gdb - the SIGTERM kill there shows the unblocked case - then type the nasm stub and the exploit in vi, assemble with nasm, and run the sweep.
The shell comes up as manpage two, and the password file reads back m two u P l t j q C J.
